why:
I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Some conditions ask for more than the words do.

Check 1 requires each `<msg>` to be "that row's JSON.parse message with newlines turned into spaces". Line 1 only says `<error>` must match the single-file behaviour before the change, so the test should compare against lint's output. The check's own run step even says to do that, but the PASS condition pins a specific message source instead.

Check 5 requires the README to show the exact `<file> [<file> ...]` string and to describe `-` as stdin. Line 5 only says the README "documents the usage", so this is an exact-wording rule.

Check 4 also adds "the existing lint tests pass", which "lint(text) … is unchanged" does not require.

These stricter tests belong under Advisory, not in PASS/FAIL conditions, so the criterion fails.
